explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Matthew says Mary "was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 1:18). Later the angel says it again, that the One conceived in her "is from the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 1:20). Same source both times, and it's not a surprise to heaven.

Zechariah is a priest, and Luke tells us he and his wife Elizabeth were going to have a son named John (Luke 1:13). That's a different story, friend. In Matthew's account, the text says Mary was found with child "through the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 1:18). Easy to mix up when there are so many baby announcements going around.

Elijah was a prophet in Israel, but he's not in this passage at all. Matthew 1:18 says Mary "was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit." No prophet, no priest, just the Holy Spirit. I once mixed up a sprinkle jar with a salt jar, so I'm not judging.

Right on the money, baker. Matthew 1:19 says Joseph "resolved to divorce her quietly." The text tells us he was a righteous man and unwilling to disgrace Mary publicly. I think he was trying to walk a very narrow road with a very heavy heart.

Close, but marrying is where Joseph ends up, not where he starts. At this point he "resolved to divorce her quietly" (Matthew 1:19). The marrying part comes after the angel speaks in the dream, when Joseph "embraced Mary as his wife" (Matthew 1:24). The story has a turn coming, friend.

Hiding sounds like a quiet move, so I get the pick. But the text says Joseph "resolved to divorce her quietly" (Matthew 1:19). The quiet part is how he'd do it. The word is divorce, and it was his plan until the angel showed up.

That's the one, baker. Matthew says "an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph had been pondering, and then the message came while he slept. Most of my best ideas come when I'm asleep too, but mine are about cookie shapes.

Nice guess, but the temple courts aren't in this scene. The text says the angel "appeared to him in a dream" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph was getting this message in his sleep, not out in public. Nobody in the courts saw a thing.

Fields do come up with angels in the Bible, but not here. Matthew 1:20 says the angel of the Lord "appeared to him in a dream." Joseph didn't have to go anywhere to get the message. He just had to lie down.

Not quite, friend. The angel says the opposite: "do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife, for the One conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 1:20). So Joseph's plan to divorce her quietly is not what the angel tells him to do. It's a full turnaround, and I'd have needed a minute to sit down.

Yes, baker. Joseph had resolved to divorce Mary quietly, but the angel says, "do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife" (Matthew 1:20). The angel gives the reason too: the One conceived in her "is from the Holy Spirit." So the angel doesn't tell him to go ahead. He tells him to take Mary home.

explanations.answer: He will save His people from their sins
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The angel says, "you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins" (Matthew 1:21). The reason for the name is right there in the same sentence. That's the whole mission, wrapped up in a name.

explanations.answer: He will rebuild the temple in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: That's a big job, but it's not the reason the angel gives. The angel says the name is Jesus "because He will save His people from their sins" (Matthew 1:21). Saving from sins is the point of the name. A building project isn't mentioned at all, friend.

explanations.answer: He will lead His people home from exile
explanations.explanation: Exile does show up in this passage, in the family list, where Matthew counts the generations "from the exile to the Christ" (Matthew 1:17). But the angel's reason for the name is different. He says, "He will save His people from their sins" (Matthew 1:21). It's easy to grab the answer that's closest to the last thing you read.

Right, baker. The words say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son" (Matthew 1:23). Matthew tells us these words come from the prophet, and the Lord said them through him. Now you know why I said lean in.

A widow is someone with a story of her own in the Bible, like Naomi in the book of Ruth. But the prophet's words here say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son" (Matthew 1:23). The word is virgin, friend. Good thing you can check it.

Queen has a royal ring to it, and Jesus does come from the family of David the king (Matthew 1:1). But the prophet's words don't use that word. They say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son" (Matthew 1:23). Fancy title, wrong blank.

That's it, baker. The text says they will call Him Immanuel "(which means, 'God with us')" (Matthew 1:23). Matthew gives us the meaning himself, right in the verse. Read that name slowly, friend. It's a good one to sit with.

That one has a nice ring to it, but it's not what Matthew says. He tells us Immanuel means "God with us" (Matthew 1:23). He puts the meaning in parentheses so nobody has to guess. Good thing, because I would have.

That's a meaning for a different name, and I won't pretend I remember which. What matters here is that Matthew tells us what Immanuel means: "God with us" (Matthew 1:23). He gives the meaning right in the verse. No guessing needed.

Yes, baker. Matthew says that when Joseph woke up, "he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and embraced Mary as his wife" (Matthew 1:24). The text doesn't mention any delay. He heard the word, and he did it.

explanations.answer: Tells the priests what he saw
explanations.explanation: That would be a reasonable move for a man with a lot on his mind. But the text doesn't say Joseph told anyone anything. It says he "did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and embraced Mary as his wife" (Matthew 1:24). He went straight to doing what he was told.

Not here, friend. Joseph's earlier plan was to divorce her quietly (Matthew 1:19), but after the dream, the text says he "embraced Mary as his wife" (Matthew 1:24). Nobody was sent anywhere. Mary stayed right by his side.
